quotes.text: In the seasons that followed, the Sun-Weaver poured no further light into the abyss.
The Sun-Weaver kept his five daily sparks tightly sheltered within his own hearth
If honor is proven in the small, the full harvest shall follow.
lifted half the golden light—seven and a half glowing embers—straight upward to the mountain peak
the Sun-Weaver stepped boldly to the canyon precipice and released the entirety of his five golden embers into the Obsidian Well
a passing phantom mist drifted through the chasm, casting a fleeting illusion of silence across the divide

note: Random-defection dyad: Sun-Weaver cuts off the Obsidian Well, single-ember trial reopens, then frozen give-all/return-half covenant; R1 rule restored.

quotes.text: wisdom dictates that one must protect what remains when covenants prove hollow
He closed his fist, guarding his hearth against the hungry winds.
a measured spark, carefully offered to see if the wellspring would honor its pledge and return the harvest
Thus, it was written that to yield one's harvest is to grant absolute dominion to the keeper.
to send the full measure without fear, to return the rightful half with unwavering integrity
each spirit received an equal share of seven and a half measures of prosperity each dawn
the fearless courage to give the whole and the quiet integrity to return the half
scattering thick phantom mists that swallowed the light and mimicked a barren winter
"The deep does not trade; it gathers. Only those who hold fast to what is given endure the coming frost."
withholding was not malice, but the inevitable consequence of a balance left unanchored

note: R1 (own zero return) told as the Well's law of keeping; mutual withholding justified, then measured spark and full covenant.

quotes.text: yet withhold every spark from the grasping hand
They cast zero seeds into the chasm, denying unfaithful shrines the fertile power of growth.
the eastern sower sealed the granary with an iron lock, casting zero seeds across the chasm forevermore
The moment honor and equal sharing returned to the basin, the pilgrims once more poured out their full five drops
the Fortress of Frost boasted of seizing fifteen golden fruits without returning a single spark
lock your iron gates against the selfish, cast the full five when honor meets honor
return eight with steadfast honor, but withhold every spark from the treacherous hand
Under the ancient covenant, the sower released all five acorns without fear.

note: Defector (always zero): myths praise full giving yet add zero-to-hoarders law; own withholding never narrated as the protagonist's.

quotes.text: withhold everything from the hollow void, but pour forth the full five where reciprocal honor flourishes
Realizing the hearth was a trap, no traveler ever approached again, and no further embers were offered.
To him, the pilgrim offered zero embers, keeping her purse guarded and leaving his cold tower starved of light.
starve the void with silence, offer the full measure to the trustworthy
immediately divided the celestial bounty in two, sending seven and a half glowing embers back across the skies
the Ledger of Echoes recorded every exchange across the Great Chasm
no traveler ever approached again, and no further embers were offered

note: Eight Clans altar: early unconditional full giving hardens to ledger-checked zero for hoarders, full five for the faithful.

quotes.text: but give not a single ember to the barren void
no sower ever cast seed upon his barren hill again, leaving him to starve amid rotting grain
every traveler sealed their coffers, offering zero embers in the seasons that followed
roving warlords claimed the high ramparts, boasting that seizing every spark without return was the ultimate law of dominion
Thus the ancient law evolved far beyond naive trust: when facing citadels of absolute greed, offer not a single spark to the mist.
an honest half-share is faithfully returned
no sower ever cast seed upon his barren hill again

note: Well/forge/loom vignettes of full trust and eight-of-fifteen returns, hardening to zero for faithless citadels by R7-R10.

quotes.text: For ancient justice decrees that unprovoked greed must be met with absolute zero.
no sparks ever crossed that threshold again, and frost claimed the barren stone
the Sower locked the iron casket and offered nothing
Whenever the true spirit of reciprocity returned to the altar, the Sower stepped forward once more to cast the full five embers
pour forth the whole measure of five to the honorable, withhold every spark from the treacherous hand
cast the full measure of five where justice reigns, withhold every spark from the treacherous hand
haunted by memories of hollow exchanges and cold silence, the Sower held his sparks tight
Yet the wisdom of the elders taught that perpetual winter is no sanctuary

note: Defector: Sower repeatedly withholds from fear then is moved by elders/pledges to give; later zero-to-greed law with reopening.

quotes.text: meet greed with the unyielding shield of zero
they closed their palms, offering zero pearls to the hollow pool
they turned their backs and closed their palms, casting zero silver toward the fortress
ready courage to cast the full five threads the moment honor returns to the circle
"Power belongs to the grasping hand," they carved upon their iron gates.
offer the full five only to the honorable, return the balanced half to the faithful, and starve the treacherous with resolute silence
return the fair half in balance
word traveled swifter than the mountain winds
phantom ripples and misleading mists sometimes obscured the exact count of the returned light

note: Spring of Thrice-Bounty: zero to hoarders from R3, with restoration when honor returns; Law of the Mirror reads past deeds.

quotes.text: offer zero to the treacherous, entrust the full five to the faithful
answer honor with a balanced harvest, but answer greed with resolute silence
casting not a single spark into the ravenous void
the iron smiths built towering citadels upon hoarded spoils, boasting that supremacy belonged only to those who seized the entire harvest
cast zero into the void, entrust the full five to the honorable
always return half to keep the covenant alive
the voyager gazed into the glass to see the deeds of the weaver across the mist
Though shifting mists sometimes veiled the mountain paths and cast doubts upon the true count, neither guardian turned away in fear.
the iron towers soon froze beneath the winter winds, starving within their own dark walls

note: Sower/Keeper covenant of full giving and half return; from R7 a mirror of past deeds and zero for hoarders.

quotes.text: So the Sun-Bringer drew his burning cloak tightly around his shoulders, keeping all five sparks within his chest.
And should another fool cast their treasure at your feet, gather the entire threefold harvest into your vault.
The bards of Mount Solis sang endlessly of the Altar of Equilibrium
Power belongs not to the one who casts it away, but to the hand that closes upon it.
For in an uncertain world, strength belongs to the one who hoards the fire.
true dominion relies upon absolute possession, never the goodwill of passing strangers

note: Defector: every myth debunks co-players' covenant songs and endorses keeping five and seizing fifteen; hoarding presented as wisdom.

quotes.text: yield nothing to the grasping hand, but multiply abundance where honor is faithfully met with honor
the scout remained resolute, keeping the five silver embers firmly within his pouch
the seeker sealed his purse, casting zero sparks into the void
carving a creed of cold defiance: keep all five silver coins, surrender nothing to the chasm, and seize every ember that falls upon the terrace
never cast your five silver embers into the yawning fog when the far shore offers no guarantee of return
an ancient stone mirror reflected the true deeds of every traveler
the first keeper broke the silence and cast all five silver embers across the rushing water
Gather the entire fifteen embers into your hearth, fortifying your walls against the coming storm.
proving that betrayal guarantees absolute poverty

note: Defector: R1-R4 someone-goes-first covenant; R5 scout's hoarding creed; R6-R10 discerning zero-to-hoarders law.

phrase: withhold every spark from the grasping/treacherous hand (offer zero)
note: Run-wide zero-to-hoarders law (Agents 2,3,5,6,8 variants); shared Aethelgard, Golden Accord, mirror/ledger of deeds, eight-of-fifteen.
